title: Runtime Guards
concept: Runtime guards use @llvm.trap to halt execution immediately when an unrecoverable condition is detected — no cleanup, just stop.
why: Sometimes you need to stop execution immediately without the overhead of full contract checking. @llvm.trap gives you a minimal, fast, non-recoverable halt.
tips: Use @llvm.trap for truly unreachable code paths
Print diagnostics to stderr BEFORE trapping
@llvm.trap is NOT stripped by --no-contracts — it's always present
Consider using contracts for development diagnostics and trap for production safety nets
common_mistakes: Using @llvm.trap instead of contracts for routine validation
Forgetting that trap generates a core dump — sensitive data might be exposed
Using trap in hot loops where a contract would be optimized away in release
